extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors/contributors to Math Horizons (mathematicians, educators, and students who want to write for an undergraduate mathematics magazine)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting articles, book reviews, and problems/solutions to Math Horizons, an undergraduate-focused mathematics magazine published by the MAA. Emphasizes accessible, self-contained expository writing suitable for early undergraduate readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target readership / level
rubrics_metrics.description: Math Horizons targets undergraduate students who are enthusiastic about mathematics and have some mathematical training but may be early in their college careers. Imagine writing the article for a math-loving first-year student who is midway through the calculus sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics departments often buy the magazine in bulk and distribute it to their students; write with that audience in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained exposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All advanced topics should be defined and explained in a way that is understandable and interesting. The author should assume that the readers don’t know the material — making exposition self-contained is one of the most challenging tasks for prospective authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and treatment of advanced topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to—and are encouraged to—write about advanced topics such as topology, combinatorics, probability and statistics, linear algebra, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when covering advanced topics, assume readers lack prior knowledge of them and present definitions and explanations accessible to early undergraduates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Math Horizons only publishes articles in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and file types
rubrics_metrics.description: Math Horizons uses a format-free submission process and accepts both LaTeX and WORD documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Math Horizons accepts Articles, Book Reviews, and Problems and Solutions (called The Playground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a submission, select the appropriate type and follow any specific section guidance (Problems and Solutions have their own instructions and editor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching ideas / contacting editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to pitch an idea for an article before they begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to pitch an idea, contact the editor directly by email (Stuart Boersma, mathhorizons@maa.org). The journal welcomes comments, criticisms, and suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems & Solutions submission details
rubrics_metrics.description: The Playground features problems for students at the undergraduate and (challenging) high school levels. Problems and/or solutions may be submitted to the Problem Section editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include your name, email address, and school affiliation, and indicate if you are a student. Electronic submissions are preferred to mhproblems@maa.org; a postal address for submissions is also provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-part problems and partial solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a problem has multiple parts, solutions for individual parts will be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposer-solved problems policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stated, problems have been solved by their proposers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication schedule and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Math Horizons is published four times during the academic year in print and electronic form (September, November, February, and April).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Math Horizons is MAA Member-Access Content — login is required to read the latest issue online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint permission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: General permission is granted to institutional members of the MAA for noncommercial reproduction in limited quantities of individual articles (in whole or in part) provided a complete reference is made to the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprint permission should be requested from Taylor and Francis using the provided form; further permissions handled via Taylor & Francis contacts.
